title: Congruent Figures on a Grid Core Test
description: Identify congruent figures on grids using corresponding measurements and rigid transformations.

questions.questionText: Triangle A has side lengths 3, 4, 5. Which triangle is congruent to Triangle A?
questions.correctAnswer: Triangle B with side lengths 3, 4, 5
questions.explanation: Congruent triangles have matching corresponding side lengths.

questions.questionText: A rectangle is 6 units by 4 units. Which rectangle is congruent to it?

Figure A and Figure B are congruent.
Figure B is similar but not congruent.
Figure B has different angle measures.
questions.correctAnswer: Figure A and Figure B are congruent.
questions.explanation: Congruent figures have the same size and shape, even if position or orientation changes.

options: They must be in the same location.

questions.correctAnswer: They stay the same.

questions.explanation: Congruent figures have the same size and shape, even if position or orientation changes.

questions.questionText: Figure A has vertices (1,1), (5,1), (5,4), (1,4). Figure B has vertices (-2,3), (-2,7), (-5,7), (-5,3). Which claim is best?
options: The figures are not congruent because the coordinates are different.
The figures are congruent; a rotation or reflection can change orientation while preserving side lengths.
The figures are not congruent because one side is vertical.
The figures are congruent only if all vertices are positive.
questions.correctAnswer: The figures are congruent; a rotation or reflection can change orientation while preserving side lengths.
questions.explanation: A congruence claim needs preserved corresponding distances and angle measures, or a rigid transformation sequence.
